siem-supported-platforms.statement: SIEM integrations can be added for ArcSight, IBM QRadar, Microsoft Azure Sentinel, Netmonastery DNIF, Splunk, Syslog and Sumo Logic, to transmit logs in real time (the ITDR page says event logs).

quotes: - ArcSight
- IBM QRadar
- Microsoft Azure Sentinel
- Netmonastery DNIF
- Splunk
- Syslog
- Sumo Logic
You can integrate Zscaler Deception with supported SIEM solutions to transmit logs in real time.
- ArcSight
- IBM QRadar
- Microsoft Azure Sentinel
- Netmonastery DNIF
- Splunk
- Syslog

You can integrate ITDR with supported SIEM solutions to transmit event logs in real time.

siem-list-columns.statement: The SIEM Integrations page lists Name, Type (the SIEM solution), Connector (the Service Connector forwarding logs), Source (type of log, such as Events or Audit Logs), Last Failure (the last error message, if any) and Enabled.

quotes: Name: The name of the SIEM integration.
Type: The name of the SIEM solution.
Connector: The Service Connector that is configured to forward logs to the SIEM.
Source: The type of log (e.g., Events or Audit Logs) that is forwarded to the SIEM.
Last Failure: The last error message, if any.
Enabled: The X icon indicates that the SIEM integration is disabled, and the check mark icon indicates that the SIEM integration is enabled.

sentinel-dcr-deprecated-legacy.statement: In the Deception guide, Microsoft has deprecated the legacy log ingestion method, so a Microsoft Sentinel integration configured with it must be reconfigured to use data collection rule-based log ingestion; the guide selects Sentinel DCR from the Add Integration drop-down menu.

quotes: Microsoft has deprecated the legacy log ingestion method. If you previously configured Microsoft Sentinel using this method, you must reconfigure the integration to use data collection rule-based log ingestion.
Click Add Integration, and select Sentinel DCR from the drop-down menu.

sentinel-prereqs.statement: In the Deception Sentinel guide, the integration needs the TCP protocol, a log analytics workspace with Microsoft Sentinel enabled, connectivity between the Service Connector and the Sentinel API server on TCP port 443, an Azure contributor with access to the resource group, and a sample JSON log file for events or audit logs to define the schema; the integration is proxy aware if direct network connectivity is not available.

quotes: Use the TCP protocol.
A log analytics workspace with Microsoft Sentinel is enabled.
You have network connectivity between the Service Connector and Sentinel API server on TCP port 443.
A Microsoft Azure contributor has access to the resource group.
You have a sample JSON log file for events or audit logs to define schema.
The Sentinel SIEM integration is proxy aware if direct network connectivity is not available.

sentinel-azure-objects.statement: In the Deception Sentinel DCR setup, the Region selected must match the log analytics workspace, Azure automatically appends _CL to the end of the table name, the transformation is source | extend TimeGenerated = now(), and the immutableId value and streamDeclarations name are copied from the data collection rule's JSON View.

quotes: Region: Select a region, and ensure that it matches your log analytics workspace.
Azure automatically appends _CL to the end of the name.
source | extend TimeGenerated = now()
Select the data collection rule that you created.
Click JSON View.
Copy the immutableId value
Copy the streamDeclarations name

sentinel-rbac.statement: The Deception Sentinel DCR guide searches for and reviews the Monitoring Metrics Publisher role, selects the data collection rule created in the previous step, opens Access Control (IAM) and selects the application created in the previous step (for example Zscaler-Deception-Sentinel-App).

quotes: search for and review Monitoring Metrics Publisher.
Select the data collection rule that you created in the previous step.
select Access Control (IAM).
search for the application name that you created in the previous step (e.g., Zscaler-Deception-Sentinel-App), and click Select.

sentinel-portal-fields.statement: The Deception Sentinel DCR integration form takes Tenant ID, Client ID, Client Secret, DCR Immutable ID, DCE Endpoint (the log ingestion URI) and Stream Name, plus Use Proxy Settings if the Service Connector requires a proxy to connect to the Sentinel server.

quotes: Tenant ID: Enter the tenant ID.
Client ID: Enter the client ID you copied from the Azure portal.
Client Secret: Enter the client secret value you copied from the Azure portal.
DCR Immutable ID: Enter the immutable ID you copied from the data collection rule in the Azure portal.
DCE Endpoint: Enter the log ingestion URI you copied from the data collection endpoint in the Azure portal.
Stream Name: Enter the stream name you copied from the data collection rule in the Azure portal.
Use Proxy Settings: Enable if the Service Connector requires a proxy to connect to the Sentinel server.

itdr-sentinel-legacy.title: Whether the ITDR Sentinel Workspace ID and Primary key method is the legacy ingestion method Microsoft deprecated
itdr-sentinel-legacy.detail: The Deception guide says Microsoft deprecated the legacy log ingestion method and selects Sentinel DCR. The ITDR guide takes a Workspace ID and Primary key and selects Sentinel, and carries no deprecation note. No captured page says whether the ITDR method is the deprecated one or still supported.
